title: How do we read the letters on two different number lines?
description: Two number lines are read: one from 8 to 8.1 in ten parts, and one that starts at 4.3 with a mark every 0.05. Keeko doubts the fifth mark of the first line and thinks it is 8.5.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the size of one step first, then count steps from the left end. Watch for students who give every line steps of one tenth.

source: One line runs from 8 to 8.1 and is cut into 10 equal parts,
video_script.why: The child has found part sizes on long lines and now meets a very short line and a line with a stated step.
video_script.substitution: Find the size of one step, and add that step as many times as the mark number to the left end.
video_script.anchor: the two number lines of the book, one from 8 to 8.1 with d and e, one starting at 4.3 with f, g and h
video_script.wrong_move: Reads the fifth mark on the short line as 8.5 instead of 8.05.
video_script.payoff_line: Add one step for every mark you count

final_answer.spoken: d is eight point zero one, e is eight point zero five, f is four point three five, g is four point five and h is four point eight five

video_script.design: The two lines stay on screen, one above the other. Each mark flashes in turn as it is counted.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a line from 8 to 8.1 with d and e, and a line from 4.3 to 4.8 with f, g and h
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about two number lines.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first line runs from eight to eight point one. It has two letters.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second line starts at four point three. It has three letters. What decimal does each letter stand for?

marks.think: Keeko sits beside the two lines

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: step = the gap from one mark to the next; mark number n = left end + n steps

marks.step: the gap between two neighbouring marks glows
marks.count: marks are counted from the left end

narration: <bookmark mark='step'/>A step is the gap from one mark to the next.
<bookmark mark='count'/>To reach a mark, count its steps from the left end.

beats.on_screen: Given: line 1 from 8 to 8.1 in 10 equal parts, d at the 1st mark, e at the 5th; line 2 starts at 4.3, marks every 0.05, 4.8 at the 10th mark, f at the 1st, g at the 4th, h past 4.8

marks.letters: the places of f, g and h are written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Given, a line from eight to eight point one in ten parts. The letter d is at the first mark, and e is at the fifth.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Another line starts at four point three, with a mark every zero point zero five.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>The letter f is at the first mark, and g is at the fourth. The letter h is one mark past four point eight.

beats.on_screen: To find: d, e, f, g and h
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find d, e, f, g and h.

marks.size: zero point one divided by ten is written
marks.d: d is placed one step after eight
marks.e: e is placed five steps after eight

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step one, the first line is zero point one long, in ten parts. Each step is zero point zero one.
<bookmark mark='d'/>The letter d is one step after eight, so it is eight point zero one.
<bookmark mark='e'/>The letter e is five steps after eight. Five steps make zero point zero five, so it is eight point zero five.

beats.on_screen: line 2: 10 x 0.05 = 0.5; 4.3 + 0.5 = 4.8, which fits the label

marks.ten: ten steps of zero point zero five are added
marks.fit: the label four point eight lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step two, check the second line. Ten steps of zero point zero five make zero point five.
<bookmark mark='fit'/>Four point three plus zero point five is four point eight, which fits the label.

marks.f: f is placed one step after four point three
marks.g: g is placed four steps after four point three

narration: <bookmark mark='f'/>Step three, the letter f is one step after four point three. Four point three plus zero point zero five is four point three five.
<bookmark mark='g'/>The letter g is four steps after. Four steps make zero point two, so it is four point five.

marks.h: h is placed one step past four point eight

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step four, the letter h is one step past four point eight.
Four point eight plus zero point zero five is four point eight five.

marks.first: d and e sit on their line
marks.second: f, g and h sit on their line

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Add one step for every mark you count.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The letter d is eight point zero one, and e is eight point zero five.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The letter f is four point three five, and g is four point five. The letter h is four point eight five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two lines
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: the fifth mark of line 1 is 8.5; 8.5 is far beyond the end 8.1; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the marker for 8.5 flies off the end of the line
marks.small: a step on this short line shrinks

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the fifth mark on the first line is eight point five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But that lies far beyond the end of the line, which is eight point one.
<bookmark mark='small'/>A step on this short line is much smaller than zero point one.
